goal: Our workflow's recent runs look weak - set up a review queue for the flagged traces and kick off a workflow calibration.

expected_steps.interaction: input form (Aria needs information): enter name, description, reviewers and questions from review-queues/triage-review.queue.json, then Approve
input form: enter the flagged trace_ids (from seed_traces.py) and optionally assigned_to (enqueue.json); queue_id is wired from review_queue.create and is not asked for. Then Approve

input form: enter an existing workflow_id and agent_id (from setup_subject.py; see calibrate.json), then Approve. Approving enqueues a refinement job and the plan PARKS (status running, step waiting_job) until the plan worker, or POST /aria/plans/{id}/poll, sees the job finish

notes: review_queue.add_items depends on review_queue.create (its queue_id is wired); workflow.calibrate depends on nothing. add_items and calibrate operate on EXISTING ids (traces, workflow, agent): Aria does not create them. The calibration job ends candidate_ready or applied (the plan completes), or rejected / failed / error (the plan fails with the job's reason). On a simulated deployment the job is rejected: the fake executor gives a candidate the same outputs as the baseline, so the quality gain (+0.000) is below the 0.02 it must clear.
